statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the vent anemone, metal tolerance proteins (MTPs) constitute a unique evolutionary adaptation to the high levels of Fe2+ and Mn2+ in its surroundings.
statements.evidence: Impressively, the metal tolerance proteins MTPs is a unique evolutionary response to the high concentrations of Fe 2+ and Mn 2+ present in the environments of these anemones.
statements.note: The abstract singles out the MTPs as a unique evolutionary response to the high Fe2+ and Mn2+ concentrations around these anemones.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Exposing Alvinactis idsseensis to high iron and manganese levels in the laboratory increased the expression of its MTP genes.
statements.evidence: Impressively, the metal tolerance proteins MTPs is a unique evolutionary response to the high concentrations of Fe 2+ and Mn 2+ present in the environments of these anemones.
statements.note: The MTP conclusion comes from comparative genomics; the abstract reports no exposure experiment and no measurement of MTP gene expression.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Comparative genomics revealed expanded gene families and newly evolved genes in Alvinactis idsseensis, reflecting a response to high concentrations of metal ions.
statements.evidence: Comparative genomic analyses revealed gene family expansions and gene innovations in A. idsseensis sp. nov. as a response to high concentrations of metal ions.
statements.note: Comparative genomic analyses showed gene family expansions and gene innovations in A. idsseensis, presented as a response to high metal ion concentrations.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The genome contains sensory and circadian rhythm-regulated genes that the study found to be essential for the anemone's adaptation to darkness.
statements.evidence: We also found genes associated with high concentrations of polyunsaturated fatty acids that may respond to high hydrostatic pressure and found sensory and circadian rhythm-regulated genes that were essential for adaptations to darkness.
statements.note: The abstract reports sensory and circadian rhythm-regulated genes that were essential for adapting to the darkness of the vents.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: If Megasiphon thylakos belongs to the tunicate crown group, appendicularians split from all other tunicates 50 million years earlier than molecular clocks estimate.
statements.evidence: Alternatively, a position within the crown-group indicates that the divergence between appendicularians and all other tunicates occurred 50 million years earlier than currently estimated based on molecular clocks.
statements.note: Under the alternative crown-group placement, the split between appendicularians and other tunicates would predate molecular-clock estimates by 50 million years.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Megasiphon thylakos, dated to about 500 million years ago, had a barrel-shaped body, a pair of long siphons and well-developed longitudinal muscles.
statements.evidence: Here we describe Megasiphon thylakos nov., a 500-million-year-old tunicate from the Marjum Formation of Utah, which features a barrel-shaped body with two long siphons and prominent longitudinal muscles.
statements.note: The abstract describes the 500-million-year-old M. thylakos as barrel-shaped, with two long siphons and prominent longitudinal muscles.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Fossilised larvae of Megasiphon thylakos were found alongside the adults, directly documenting a planktonic larval stage.
statements.evidence: The most likely scenario posits M. thylakos belongs to stem-group Tunicata, suggesting that a biphasic life cycle, with a planktonic larva and a sessile epibenthic adult, is ancestral for this entire subphylum.
statements.note: The biphasic life cycle is inferred from the fossil's likely phylogenetic position; the abstract never mentions preserved larvae.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Under the favoured interpretation, Megasiphon thylakos is a stem-group tunicate, implying that a biphasic life cycle with planktonic larvae and sessile adults is ancestral to all tunicates.
statements.evidence: The most likely scenario posits M. thylakos belongs to stem-group Tunicata, suggesting that a biphasic life cycle, with a planktonic larva and a sessile epibenthic adult, is ancestral for this entire subphylum.
statements.note: The abstract's most likely scenario places M. thylakos in stem-group Tunicata, which implies a biphasic life cycle is ancestral to the whole subphylum.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mutations in the human CUX2 gene cause abnormal folding of the cerebral cortex in patients.
statements.evidence: Folding of the cerebral cortex is a key aspect of mammalian brain development and evolution, and defects are linked to severe neurological disorders.
statements.note: The abstract links folding defects to neurological disorders in general and studies Cux2 only in ferret; it says nothing about human CUX2 mutations.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Altering Cux2 expression in ferret cortical progenitors modified their proliferation and the pattern of cortical folding.
statements.evidence: Manipulating Cux2 expression in cortical progenitors changed their proliferation and the folding pattern in ferret, caused by selective transcriptional changes as revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing analyses.
statements.note: Manipulating Cux2 in ferret cortical progenitors changed both their proliferation and the folding pattern, through selective transcriptional changes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In ferret, the transcriptomic protomap that prefigures cortical folds is already emerging at early embryonic stages and involves cell-fate signaling pathways.
statements.evidence: Our results show that the transcriptomic protomap begins to emerge at early embryonic stages, and it involves cell-fate signaling pathways.
statements.note: The results show the folding protomap starting to emerge at early embryonic stages and involving cell-fate signaling pathways.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mapping H3K27ac across prospective folds and fissures revealed developmental restriction of cell fate and implicated known regulators such as the transcription factor Cux2.
statements.evidence: The H3K27ac landscape reveals developmental cell-fate restriction and engages known developmental regulators, including the transcription factor Cux2
statements.note: The H3K27ac landscape revealed cell-fate restriction and engaged known developmental regulators, Cux2 among them.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across angiosperms, style-length polymorphism originated independently many times and was associated with radially symmetric, tubular flowers pollinated by long-tongued insects.
statements.evidence: Using phylogenetic and comparative analyses across the angiosperms, we show numerous independent origins of style-length polymorphism associated with actinomorphic, tubular flowers with a low number of sex organs, stamens fused to the corolla, and pollination by long-tongued insects.
statements.note: Phylogenetic comparative analyses showed numerous independent origins of style-length polymorphism, associated with actinomorphic tubular flowers and long-tongued insect pollinators.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The trait associations found support Darwin's pollination-precision hypothesis as the basis for repeated, convergent evolution of heterostyly in flowering plants.
statements.evidence: These associations provide support for the Darwinian pollination-precision hypothesis as a basis for convergent evolution of heterostyly across angiosperms.
statements.note: The abstract concludes that the floral associations support Darwin's pollination-precision hypothesis for the convergent evolution of heterostyly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The updated census increased the number of known heterostylous and other style-length polymorphic taxa by 20%, to 247 genera in 34 families.
statements.evidence: Here we update the number of heterostylous and other style-length polymorphic taxa to 247 genera belonging to 34 families, notably expanding known cases by 20%.
statements.note: The update raised the count to 247 genera in 34 families, expanding the known cases by 20%.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Heterostylous plant species set more seed than closely related species with a single flower morph.
statements.evidence: Darwin hypothesised that heterostyly evolved to promote outcrossing through efficient pollen transfer between morphs involving different areas of a pollinator's body
statements.note: The study tests floral-trait associations across a phylogeny; it reports no measurements of seed set or reproductive success.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Co-opted ERVs derive from escapee elements that have lost key sequences needed both for TRIM28 restriction and for autonomous retrotransposition.
statements.evidence: In sum, co-opted ERVs stem from genetic escapees that have lost vital sequences required for both TRIM28 restriction and autonomous retrotransposition.
statements.note: The abstract concludes that co-opted ERVs come from escapees that lost the sequences required for TRIM28 restriction and autonomous retrotransposition.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: About 15% of IAPs, termed escapees, differ significantly in sequence from the 190 bp signal-peptide region through which TRIM28 silences IAPs.
statements.evidence: Transcriptional silencing via TRIM28 maps to a 190 bp sequence encoding the intracisternal A-type particle (IAP) signal peptide, which confers retrotransposition activity. A subset of "escapee" IAPs (∼15%) exhibits significant genetic divergence from this sequence.
statements.note: About 15% of IAPs, the escapees, show significant genetic divergence from the 190 bp TRIM28-targeted signal-peptide sequence.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Escapee IAPs also evade TRIM28 repression in adult mouse neurons.
statements.evidence: Escapee IAPs, in contrast, evade repression in both cell types, resulting in their transcriptional derepression, particularly in NPCs.
statements.note: The study examined only embryonic stem cells and neural progenitor cells; adult neurons are not mentioned.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Within the U3 region of the IAP long terminal repeat, a 47 bp stretch was confirmed to function as an enhancer.
statements.evidence: We validate the enhancer function of a 47 bp sequence within the U3 region of the long terminal repeat (LTR)
statements.note: The study validated the enhancer function of a 47 bp sequence in the U3 region of the LTR.

statements.evidence: phenotypes of CRISPR/Cas9-induced mutants showed that double hoxb13a and hoxc13a mutants fail to form a caudal fin
statements.note: Double hoxb13a and hoxc13a mutants failed to form a caudal fin.
